bullets.text: Machine learning involves teaching computers to learn from data.
It contrasts with giving computers explicit, predefined rules.
The lecture introduces different types of machine learning.
System is trained on labeled data, where outputs are known.
Example: Identifying spam emails based on labeled examples.
Model learns patterns to predict outcomes for new, unseen data.
Common algorithms include decision trees, support vector machines, and neural networks.
System discovers patterns in data without pre-existing labels.
Example: Grouping customers into segments based on purchasing behavior.
K-means is a classic algorithm used for clustering.
An agent learns by interacting with an environment.
Learning occurs through feedback or rewards received from actions.
Applications include training AI for video games or robot control.
Overfitting: Model memorizes training data, leading to poor performance on new data.
Bias: Occurs when the training data is unbalanced or not representative, affecting fairness.
These challenges require careful model design and data preparation.
Healthcare: Used for disease prediction and diagnosis.
Finance: Applied in fraud detection systems.
Self-driving cars: Essential for object recognition and navigation.
The next lecture will delve into how to evaluate machine learning models.
It will cover essential evaluation metrics for model performance.
Specific metrics include accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.
